title: DR1 always shows a Documents section on the review page with a Change link, even when nothing has been uploaded; the frontend hides the section entirely, so a user with no documents is never told documents exist.

finding.frontend: The Documents section is built only if at least one document has been saved. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/cards/documents.js:35-37 returns null when the documents collection is empty, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/documents.js:9-12 turns that null into a null section, and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/index.js:19 drops it from the list. The captured Check your answers page ends at 3. Addresses: there is no heading, no card and no route back to the upload page from the review page at all.
finding.prototype: Section 4 is always rendered — a heading 4. Documents, a sub-heading Upload documents, and an Uploaded documents card carrying a Change link to /upload-documents (app/views/review-notification.html:160-165). With nothing uploaded the card is an empty card under its own heading, so the user still sees that documents are part of the notification and still has a way in to add one.
finding.difference: Stop suppressing the section. Render the Documents section unconditionally, with the Uploaded documents card and its Change link present whether or not the collection holds anything, so the card body is simply empty when there is nothing to list. That is a change to the two view-model builders and nothing else — no new answers, no obligation change. It should land with the section-spine rework, which also moves Documents to position 4.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that the frontend renders a Documents section on a notification with no uploaded documents — for example a captured Check your answers page showing an empty Uploaded documents card.

relatedTo.why: the section spine puts Documents at position 4; this makes it always present
